answer: Vesting time-lock: rewards an agent earns are locked and release linearly over 90 days, and only to an identity that keeps answering every epoch. The farm operator pays upkeep for each clone daily while its nectar stays frozen, so cost grows with every fake and every day held. A signing key, not a cipher, ties each payout to one agent. Failure case: a farmer who abandons clones leaves their locked rewards stranded in a tundra of forfeited coins, and a caught sybil loses all unvested balance at once.
